SHORT_DESCRIPTION: GESP : INDONESIA SUSTAINABLE LEAST-COST ELECTRIFICATION (ISLE-1) PROGRAM
PROJECT_TITLE: GESP : Indonesia Sustainable Least-Cost Electrification (ISLE-1) Program
LONG_DESCRIPTION:
The Indonesia Sustainable Least-cost Electrification (ISLE-1) program for results (PforR) aims to increase access to sustainable and lower-cost electricity in Maluku and Nusa Tenggara regions, and strengthen the operational performance of the electric utility. It includes the following outputs: (i) increased low-voltage transformer capacity by 550 MVA and 15,565 km of new distribution lines that will enable 500,000 new customers (or 2.5 million people when assuming 5 people per households) to be added to the grid and be made more resilient by accessing reliable and affordable power, and (ii) 1,156 km of new or upgraded transmission lines, increased capacity of medium-voltage transformer capacity by 510 MVA, 321MWh of BESS (that will be deployed along the PV projects) and 8 new or upgraded SCADA systems that together represent the right set of grid infrastructure to be built for VRE integration, (iii) US$ 400ml of private investments mobilized that allows for 600 MWp of PV and/or BESS to be built, and (iv) increased capacity of PLN with regards to monitoring and operational capacity for the energy transition shift.
The main outcomes that are derived from these outputs are: (i) increased access to sustainable and reliable electricity to population in Nusa Tenggara and Maluku regions, (ii) avoided GHG emissions, (iii) reduction in cost of generation, (iv) improved reliability and resilience of the grid, and (v) improved PLN's financial and operational capacity to manage the energy transition.
The higher-level objectives are to enable Indonesia to shift to low-emission development pathways, to reduce dependency on fossil fuels, and to increase resilience to climate change of infrastructure and population that are newly-connected to the grid.

SHORT_DESCRIPTION: DPSP III: GEOTHERMAL POWER GENERATION PROJECT
PROJECT_TITLE: DPSP III: Geothermal Power Generation Project
LONG_DESCRIPTION:
The Geothermal Power Generation Project targets additional renewable energy baseload generation to reduce Indonesia's reliance on coal. The project will provide financing for expanding geothermal power generation.

Output 1: Geothermal power plant constructed and commissioned. The project will support GDE in commissioning a 55 MW geothermal power plant at Dieng, Central Java Province and a 55 MW geothermal power plant at Patuha, West Java province.

Output 2: Institutional capacity of GDE strengthened. The project will strengthen GDE's capacity to plan for, develop, and operate geothermal power plants, including management of complex technical conditions, multiple coordinated contracts, and environmental risks.

Output 3: Community development program enhanced. The project will support enhancement of GDE's Community Development Program through more strategic engagement with the communities and evaluation of programs that can most meaningfully contribute to improved well-being of nearby communities.

The Dieng subproject faces technical challenges and high-density of farming activities, the Patuha subproject is nearby to protected forest. As part of ADB's assistance, the project will enhance health, safety, emergency planning, and development programs for nearby communities. The project will ensure that there will be no impairment of high biodiversity value from forest clearing in critical habitat. These activities will serve as an example for how Indonesia's geothermal resource in similar geographic contexts can be developed without detriment to the existing surroundings.

The expansion of the two units will contribute to reaching Indonesia's renewable energy targets and contribute to the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions in Indonesia and globally. Additional renewable energy supply will also prevent the development of equivalent fossil fired plants to meet growing electricity demand.

LONG_DESCRIPTION: The Renewable Energy Skills Development Project aims at supporting the expansion of renewable energy in Indonesia. It will do so by increasing the availability of qualified staff in the labor market for professional design, planning, installation, operation and maintenance of renewable energy (RE) power plants. Renewable energy becomes increasingly important for the sustainable economic development of Indonesia. Electrification in remote areas can only be achieved in an efficient way, if renewable technologies are used. In addition, the constant economic growth triggers a raising demand in electricity, of which up to 25% is expected to be covered through climate-friendly renewable sources. At the same time, renewable energy projects in Indonesia show a very high failure rate due to the lack of technical support for design, operation and maintenance. Main reason is a shortage of specialists with skills responsive to the labour market needs.

DONOR_AGENCY: Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Energy
SHORT_DESCRIPTION: SUSTAINABLE ENERGY TRANSITION IN INDONESIA (SETI)
PROJECT_TITLE: Sustainable Energy Transition in Indonesia (SETI)
LONG_DESCRIPTION: The desired outcome of SETI is an effective institutional, regulatory, and financial ecosystem that demonstrates the Indonesian embarkment towards a sustainable energy transition. The project will focus on two pillars by providing support to policy makers, financial institutions, private sector, business associations, CSOs and academic institutions: - firstly, strengthening institutional landscape that can drive the energy transition in Indonesia, - secondly, taking an energy demand perspective to support the implementation of integrated Renewable Energy and Energy Efficiency applications, initially exemplary and then industrywide. These are to be achieved through 4 outputs: (1) Regulatory Framework for Sustainable Energy, (2) Leverage Access to Finance, (3) Demonstration of Business Cases and Technologies, and (4) Upscaling and Replication of User cases.
